scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements of a water proof multipurpose rain poncho with convertibility as a bivouac (temporary shelter) and a pouch to pack the poncho (referred as 'poncho' and 'pouch' respectively) [1]. It does not specify the general appearance, feel, or similar aesthetic characteristics [1].

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Statutory Quality Control Orders (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, mandate that protective and technical textiles intended for public, domestic, or institutional use must carry the Bureau of Indian Standards Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Products manufactured solely for export are exempt if they conform to foreign buyers' specifications. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polyamide outdoor equipment.

requirements.detail: Every water proof rain poncho and its pouch conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L) on a secure label.

The fabric used for constructing the poncho and its pouch must be woven from polyamide (Nylon 6 or Nylon 66) conforming to IS 667, finished with a Polyurethane (PU) coating analyzed in accordance with Annex B.
The finished poncho must measure 2120 + 20 mm in length and 1620 + 20 mm in width. It must be fabricated utilizing a base fabric of width 1800 + 20 mm.

The outer shell of the poncho must feature six pockets secured by 25 ± 1 mm wide hook and loop fasteners conforming to IS 8156. Each pocket must contain a braided polyamide filament yarn cord attached internally. An additional patch pocket (with cord) measuring 250 mm wide by 190 mm high must be provided on the inner back face.

The poncho must feature brass sail-type eyelets of size 30 L with bronzed washers conforming to IS 4084 placed at each corner and the center fold. It must also feature 8 sets of cage-type size 3/3 snap fasteners conforming to IS 4741.

The packing pouch must be made of single-layer finished PU-coated polyamide fabric measuring 300 ± 10 mm in length by 250 ± 10 mm in width. It must be equipped with a 210 ± 10 mm slide fastener, two nylon loops, and a single folded PU-coated polyamide handle (pouch hanging loop) of 10 ± 1 mm width and 150 ± 10 mm loop length.

The 25 ± 1 mm wide nylon tape used for the loops of the pouch must be woven on a needle loom with a warp count of 850 denier, binding warp count of 850 denier, and weft count of 450 denier polyamide yarn. The weave must feature 203 total ends (175 warp ends + 28 binding warp ends) and 340 picks per dm.
Assembly must employ lock stitching with a minimum density of 4 stitches per cm. The sewing thread must be polyamide of variety No. L2 conforming to IS 4229.

Permissible tolerances on poncho and pouch components are strictly restricted by size: up to 10 mm (±0.5 mm); above 10 to 30 mm (±1.0 mm); above 30 to 50 mm (±2.0 mm); above 50 to 80 mm (±4.0 mm); above 80 to 100 mm (±6.0 mm); above 100 to 500 mm (±10.0 mm); and above 500 to 2000 mm (±20.0 mm).
Finished assemblies must be evenly stitched, free from missed stitches, holes, cuts, puckering, tackiness, crinkling, or rustling sounds. The sewing thread must not bleed color under washing.

A lot for conformance inspection is defined as completed ponchos of the same size, type, and assemblies produced in one facility using the same processes and materials, offered for delivery at one time.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17286 : 2019 is the strict national Indian Standard specification governing water proof multi-purpose rain ponchos designed to convert into temporary field bivouacs (shelters). Developed by the Textiles Protective Clothing Sectional Committee (TXD 32), it mandates the use of highly durable polyamide (Nylon 6 or Nylon 66) woven base fabrics with a Polyurethane (PU) coating to establish complete water barrier protection. The standard outlines precise dimensional, pocket, and closure parameters—including brass eyelets, aramid or polyamide cords, and snap fasteners—and specifies the design of a matching carrying pouch with a woven nylon handle tape. Quality assurance teams must verify dimensional stability, lock stitching density (minimum 4 stitches per cm), and complete freedom from visual defects to ensure rugged, reliable utility for defense and emergency personnel [1, 4, 5, 8].
